rationale:
The agent correctly verified the user (name + zip matched a single account), accessed only the user’s own orders, and used tools to check item and variant availability. They performed the requested actions accurately: updated the pending order’s shipping address to the New York address from order #W3445693, modified the silicone watch to a metal white variant in order #W4219264 with the correct refund, and initiated an exchange for the delivered air purifier to the large HEPA model with night mode and noted a price difference.

However, the policy requires the agent to state the exact change and obtain explicit user confirmation before any order-changing write. The agent executed two changes without prior explicit confirmation: (1) updating the shipping address for #W6729841 after the user indicated which prior order to use, but without restating the exact address and asking to proceed; and (2) initiating the exchange on delivered order #W3445693 without first confirming the exact replacement variant and acknowledging the price difference before submitting the exchange. Only the watch modification had explicit confirmation before the write. Because of these confirmation lapses, the conversation does not meet the pass bar despite otherwise correct actions.
